chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Dhubyan ibn Hakim al-Awdi, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Nuymari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked about a man who has a dispute with his brother regarding a right, so they agree on two men to act as arbitrators between them. They arbitrate, but differ in their ruling. He (the Imam) said: 'How can they differ?' I said: 'Each of the two arbitrators ruled in favor of the party who chose him.' He said: 'Look to the more just of the two and the more knowledgeable in the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and his ruling is implemented.'

key_terms.أَعْدَلِهِمَا: The more just of the two
key_terms.أَفْقَهِهِمَا: The more knowledgeable in fiqh/jurisprudence of the two

ai.seo_question: How to resolve conflicting arbitrator rulings in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the resolution mechanism for conflicting arbitral awards by prioritizing the criterion of *adl* (justice) and *fiqh* (juridical depth) over the parties' initial preferences. This establishes a hierarchical standard in Shia jurisprudence where the superior scholar's ruling prevails, ensuring legal consistency in private dispute resolution. The emphasis on 'more just' reflects the Shia principle that moral integrity is a prerequisite for authoritative legal interpretation.
